children: Crude futures are mixed in light U.S. Black Friday trading with the market watching shipping risks in the Middle East and awaiting Sunday's meeting of OPEC and its allies to discuss output policy for 2027. "Long-running tensions within the group may surface over output quota decisions," and disputes among members could weaken the group's pricing power, Hamad Hussain of Capital Economics says in a note. "A more fractious and less cohesive OPEC+ will lead to greater oil price volatility and skew the balance of risks towards lower oil prices over time," he adds. WTI is up 0.5% at $84.09 a barrel and Brent is down 1.2% at $95.42 a barrel ahead of Monday's January contract expiry. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
